title.en: Volume 117 Biographies 42: Pei, Liu, Wei, Li, Ji
title.raw: 卷一百一十七 列傳第四十二 裴劉魏李吉 Volume 117 Biographies 42: Pei, Liu, Wei, Li, Ji

sentences.zh: 裴劉魏李吉

translations.literal: Pei, Liu, Wei, Li, Ji
translations.idiomatic: Pei, Liu, Wei, Li, and Ji

sentences.zh: ◎裴劉魏李吉

translations.literal: ◎ Pei, Liu, Wei, Li, Ji
translations.idiomatic: Pei, Liu, Wei, Li, and Ji

sentences.zh: 裴炎，字子隆，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Yan, courtesy name Zilong, was a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan, styled Zilong, came from Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寬厚，寡言笑，有奇節。

translations.literal: He was generous and steady, sparing of speech and laughter, and possessed extraordinary integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded and steady, spoke little and laughed less, and bore a singular moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 補弘文生，休澣，它生或出遊，炎讀書不廢。

translations.literal: He was appointed a student of the Hongwen Academy. On rest days, when other students went out to roam, Yan never ceased reading.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed a Hongwen Academy student, he kept to his books on rest days while his fellows went out to wander.

sentences.zh: 有司欲薦狀，以業未就，辭不舉，服勤十年，尤通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: When the authorities wished to recommend him with a formal petition, he declined because his studies were not yet complete; he served diligently for ten years and became especially versed in the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities sought to recommend him with a formal petition, he declined because his work was unfinished. After ten years of tireless study, he mastered the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 舉明經及第。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and received his degree.

sentences.zh: 補濮州司倉參軍，歷御史、起居舍人，浸遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary of the Si Cang section in Puzhou, then served as censor and diarist-attendant, and was gradually promoted to vice minister of the Huangmen.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretary of the Si Cang section in Puzhou, then as censor and diarist-attendant, rising by degrees to vice minister of the Huangmen.

sentences.zh: 調露二年，同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiaolu, he became one of the Three Chiefs of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tiaolu era, he was made one of the Three Chiefs of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 進拜侍中。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted further to attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸東都，留皇太子京師，以炎調護。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong visited the Eastern Capital, he left the crown prince in the capital and put Yan in charge of attending and protecting him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong went to the Eastern Capital, he left the crown prince in the capital and entrusted Yan with his care.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，太子監國，詔炎與劉齊賢、郭正一於東宮平章政事，及大漸，受遺輔太子，是為中宗。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, the crown prince supervised the state. An edict appointed Yan, Liu Qixian, and Guo Zhengyi to jointly handle state affairs at the Eastern Palace. When the emperor's illness became critical, they received his final testament to assist the crown prince, who became Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, the crown prince supervised the realm. An edict named Yan, Liu Qixian, and Guo Zhengyi to deliberate on state affairs at the Eastern Palace. As the emperor's illness turned critical, they received his deathbed charge to assist the crown prince, who then ascended as Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 改中書令。

translations.literal: He was changed to chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舊，宰相議事門下省，號政事堂，長孫無忌以司空、房玄齡以仆射、魏徵以太子太師皆知門下省事，至炎，以中書令執政事筆，故徙政事堂於中書省。

translations.literal: Formerly, when chancellors deliberated on affairs at the Chancellery, the place was called the Hall of Administration. Sun Wuji as minister of works, Fang Xuanling as vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and Wei Zheng as grand tutor of the crown prince all knew Chancellery affairs. When Yan came to office as chief of the Secretariat wielding the brush of administration, the Hall of Administration was moved to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, chancellors deliberated at the Chancellery in what was called the Hall of Administration. Sun Wuji as minister of works, Fang Xuanling as vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and Wei Zheng as grand tutor of the crown prince had all handled Chancellery business. Under Yan, the chief of the Secretariat held the administrative brush, and so the Hall of Administration was moved to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中宗欲以後父韋玄貞為侍中及授乳媼子五品官，炎固執不從，帝怒曰：「我意讓國與玄貞，豈不可？

translations.literal: Zhongzong wished to make his father-in-law Wei Xuanzhen attendant-in-ordinary and to grant fifth-rank posts to the sons of his wet nurse. Yan firmly refused. The emperor angrily said, "I mean to yield the realm to Xuanzhen—would that not be permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong wished to appoint his father-in-law Wei Xuanzhen attendant-in-ordinary and grant fifth-rank posts to his wet nurse's sons. Yan stood firm and refused. The emperor flared up: "I mean to yield the empire to Xuanzhen—would that not be allowed?

sentences.zh: 何惜侍中邪？」

translations.literal: Why begrudge the post of attendant-in-ordinary?"
translations.idiomatic: Why quibble over the post of attendant-in-ordinary?

sentences.zh: 炎懼，因與武後謀廢帝。

translations.literal: Yan feared this and therefore joined Empress Wu in plotting to depose the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, alarmed, joined Empress Wu in plotting to depose the emperor.

sentences.zh: 後命炎洎劉祎之率羽林將軍程務挺、張虔勖勒兵入宮，宣太后令，扶帝下殿，帝曰：「我何罪？」

translations.literal: The empress ordered Yan and Liu Yizhi to lead the Yulin generals Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu with troops into the palace, proclaim the empress dowager's order, and escort the emperor down from the hall. The emperor said, "What crime have I committed?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress ordered Yan and Liu Yizhi to lead Yulin generals Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu with troops into the palace, proclaim the empress dowager's command, and bring the emperor down from the throne. The emperor cried, "What crime have I committed?

sentences.zh: 後曰：「以天下與玄貞，安得無罪？」

translations.literal: The empress said, "To give the realm to Xuanzhen—how could that be without guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress replied, "To give the empire to Xuanzhen—how could that be guiltless?"

sentences.zh: 乃廢帝為盧陵王，更立豫王為皇帝。

translations.literal: They then deposed the emperor as Prince of Luling and installed Prince Yu as emperor instead.
translations.idiomatic: They deposed him as Prince of Luling and enthroned Prince Yu in his place.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，封永清縣男。

translations.literal: For his merit in settling the succession, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongqing.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in fixing the succession, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yongqing.

sentences.zh: 後已持政，稍自肆，於是武承嗣請立七廟，追王其先，炎諫曰：「太后天下母，以盛德臨朝，宜存至公，不容追王祖考，示自私。

translations.literal: After the empress had taken power, she gradually grew unrestrained. Thereupon Wu Chengsi requested the establishment of seven ancestral temples and ennoblement of his forebears. Yan remonstrated, "The empress dowager is mother to the realm. With her great virtue she holds court. She should preserve utmost fairness and must not ennoble her grandfather and father, lest she appear selfish.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress held power, she grew ever bolder. Wu Chengsi then asked to establish seven ancestral temples and ennoble his forebears. Yan remonstrated: "Your Majesty is mother to the realm and governs with great virtue. You should preserve absolute fairness. You must not ennoble your grandfather and father, for that would show self-interest.

sentences.zh: 且獨不見呂氏事乎！」

translations.literal: Have you alone not seen what happened with the Lü clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen what became of the Lü clan!

sentences.zh: 後曰：「呂氏之王，權屬生人，今追崇先世，在亡跡異，安得同哉！」

translations.literal: The empress said, "When the Lü clan was ennobled, power still belonged to the living. Now to honor past generations is a different matter from what was done then—how can the cases be the same!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress answered, "When the Lü were ennobled, power still rested with the living. To honor ancestors now is a matter of the dead, not the same at all—how can you equate them?"

sentences.zh: 炎曰：「蔓草難圖，漸不可長。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "Spreading weeds are hard to uproot; what grows gradually must not be allowed to grow long."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Weeds are hard to root out once they spread. What grows by degrees must not be indulged."

sentences.zh: 後不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The empress was displeased and dismissed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was displeased and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 承嗣又諷太后誅韓王元嘉、魯王靈夔，以絕宗室望，劉祎之、韋仁約畏默不敢言，炎獨固爭，後愈銜怒。

translations.literal: Chengsi also urged the empress dowager to execute Prince of Han Yuanjia and Prince of Lu Lingkai to cut off hope among the imperial clan. Liu Yizhi and Wei Renyue, in fear, kept silent and dared not speak. Yan alone argued stubbornly, and the empress grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi also urged the empress dowager to execute the Prince of Han, Yuanjia, and the Prince of Lu, Lingkai, to extinguish hope among the imperial clan. Liu Yizhi and Wei Renyue, afraid, kept silent. Yan alone contested the matter stubbornly, and the empress's resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賜爵河東縣侯。

translations.literal: Before long, he was granted the title Marquis of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was granted the title Marquis of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 豫王雖為帝，未嘗省天下事。

translations.literal: Although Prince Yu was emperor, he had never attended to the affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Though Prince Yu sat on the throne, he had never handled the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 炎謀乘太后出遊龍門，以兵執之，還政天子。

translations.literal: Yan plotted to seize the empress dowager with troops when she went out to visit Longmen and restore power to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yan plotted to seize the empress dowager by force when she went out to Longmen and restore rule to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，太后不出而止。

translations.literal: It happened that prolonged rain kept the empress dowager from going out, and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rain kept the empress dowager indoors, and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業兵興，後議討之，炎曰：「天子年長矣，不豫政，故豎子有辭。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingye raised troops, the empress discussed suppressing him. Yan said, "The Son of Heaven is already grown, yet does not govern. That is why this stripling has grounds to speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingye raised arms, the empress discussed suppressing him. Yan said, "The Son of Heaven is already grown, yet does not govern. That is why this upstart has words to justify himself.

sentences.zh: 今若復子明辟，賊不討而解。」

translations.literal: If you now restore the son and clarify the throne, the rebels will disperse without being attacked."
translations.idiomatic: If you now restore the son and make the succession clear, the rebels will dissolve without a fight.

sentences.zh: 御史崔詧曰：「炎受顧托，身總大權，聞亂不討，乃請太后歸政，此必有異圖。」

translations.literal: Censor Cui Cha said, "Yan received the dying charge and personally holds great power. Hearing of rebellion, he does not suppress it, yet asks the empress dowager to return power. This must mean he has some other design."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cui Cha said, "Yan received the emperor's dying charge and holds supreme power himself. Hearing of rebellion, he does not suppress it, yet asks the empress dowager to return rule. He must harbor some other design."

sentences.zh: 後乃捕炎送詔獄，遣御史大夫騫味道、御史魚承曄參鞫之。

translations.literal: The empress then had Yan arrested and sent to the imperial prison, dispatching vice censor-in-chief Qian Weidao and censor Yu Chengyao to join in the interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had Yan seized and sent to the imperial prison, dispatching vice censor-in-chief Qian Weidao and censor Yu Chengyao to examine him.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎胡元範曰：「炎社稷臣，有功於國，悉心事上，天下所知，臣明其不反。」

translations.literal: Fengge vice minister Hu Yuanfan said, "Yan is a minister of the altars of soil and grain. He has merit for the state and serves the sovereign with full devotion. All the realm knows this. Your subject knows he did not rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Fengge vice minister Hu Yuanfan said, "Yan is a pillar of the state. His service to the throne is known throughout the realm. I know he did not rebel.

sentences.zh: 納言劉齊賢、左衛率蔣儼繼辨之，後曰：「炎反有端，顧卿未知耳。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance officer Liu Qixian and Left Guard commander Jiang Yan also argued on his behalf in succession. The empress said, "Yan's rebellion has its grounds—you simply do not yet know them."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officer Liu Qixian and Left Guard commander Jiang Yan argued for him in turn. The empress said, "Yan's rebellion has its grounds—you simply do not yet know them."

sentences.zh: 元範、齊賢曰：「若炎反，臣輩亦反矣。」

translations.literal: Yuanfan and Qixian said, "If Yan rebelled, then we too have rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan and Qixian said, "If Yan rebelled, then we have rebelled too."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「朕知炎反，卿輩不反。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "I know Yan rebelled. You did not."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I know Yan rebelled. You did not."

sentences.zh: 遂斬於都亭驛。

translations.literal: He was then beheaded at Duting Station.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded at Duting Station.

sentences.zh: 炎被劾，或勉其遜辭，炎曰：「宰相下獄，理不可全。」

translations.literal: When Yan was impeached, some urged him to use humble words in his defense. Yan said, "When a chancellor is thrown into prison, it is unreasonable to expect to come out whole."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was impeached, some urged him to soften his words. He said, "When a chancellor enters prison, it is unreasonable to expect to leave whole.

sentences.zh: 卒不折節，籍其家，無擔石之贏。

translations.literal: In the end he did not bend, and when his household was inventoried there was not even a full load of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He never yielded. When his household was searched, there was not even a full load of grain to his name.

sentences.zh: 初，炎見裴行儉破突厥有功，沮薄之，乃斬降虜阿史那伏念等五十餘人，議者恨其冒克，且使國家失信四夷，以為陰禍有知雲。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan saw that Pei Xingjian had merit in defeating the Turks, he belittled and slighted him and executed more than fifty surrendered captives including Ashina Funician. Critics resented his false claim to merit and believed he had made the state lose faith among the four barbarians, thinking that hidden retribution had awareness of it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pei Xingjian won merit defeating the Turks, Yan belittled him and executed more than fifty surrendered captives, including Ashina Funician. Critics resented his false claim to glory and held that he had made the state lose the trust of the four quarters; many thought hidden retribution had taken notice.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，贈太尉、益州大都督，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Yan was posthumously made grand commandant and grand protector of Yizhou, with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Yan was posthumously ennobled grand commandant and grand protector of Yizhou, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 元範者，申州義陽人。

translations.literal: Yuanfan was a native of Yiyang in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan came from Yiyang in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 介廉有才，以炎故，流死巂州。

translations.literal: Upright, incorruptible, and talented, because of Yan he was exiled and died in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, incorruptible, and talented, he was exiled because of Yan and died in Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 炎從子伷先。

translations.literal: Yan's nephew's son was Xianxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's grandnephew was Xianxian.

sentences.zh: 伷先未冠，推蔭為太仆丞。

translations.literal: Before Xianxian had come of age, he received a yin privilege appointment as vice director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxian had not yet come of age when he entered office by inherited privilege as vice director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 炎死，坐流嶺南。

translations.literal: When Yan died, Xianxian was implicated and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's death, Xianxian was implicated and banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 上變求面陳得失，後召見，盛氣待之，曰：「炎謀反，法當誅，尚何道？」

translations.literal: He submitted a petition of grievance asking to state his views in person. The empress summoned him and received him with fierce bearing, saying, "Yan plotted rebellion and by law should be executed. What more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a petition of grievance asking to speak face to face. The empress summoned him and met him with fierce bearing. "Yan plotted rebellion and by law deserved death," she said. "What more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 伷先對曰：「陛下唐家婦，身荷先帝顧命，今雖臨朝，當責任大臣，須東宮年就德成，復子明辟，奈何遽王諸武、斥宗室？

translations.literal: Xianxian replied, "Your Majesty is a daughter-in-law of the house of Tang and received the late emperor's dying charge. Though you now hold court, you should entrust great affairs to senior ministers. When the crown prince reaches maturity in years and virtue, you should restore the son and clarify the throne. Why hastily ennoble the Wu clan and drive out the imperial house?
translations.idiomatic: Xianxian answered, "Your Majesty is a daughter-in-law of the house of Tang and received the late emperor's dying charge. Though you hold court, you should entrust great affairs to senior ministers. When the crown prince reaches maturity in years and virtue, restore the son and clarify the throne. Why so hastily ennoble the Wu and cast out the imperial clan?

sentences.zh: 炎為唐忠臣，而戮逮子孫，海內憤怨。

translations.literal: Yan was a loyal minister of Tang, yet punishment reached even his descendants. Resentment filled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been a faithful servant of Tang, yet the killing reached his descendants—and anger spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂陛下宜還太子東宮，罷諸武權。

translations.literal: This subject thinks Your Majesty should return the crown prince to the Eastern Palace and strip the Wu of power.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty should return the crown prince to the Eastern Palace and strip the Wu of power.

sentences.zh: 不然，豪傑乘時而動，不可不懼！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, bold men will seize the moment to act—you cannot but fear it!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise bold men will seize the moment. You must fear what follows!

sentences.zh: 后怒，命曳出，杖之朝堂，長流瀼州。

translations.literal: The empress was enraged and ordered him dragged out and beaten in the court hall, then sentenced him to permanent exile in Rangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, enraged, had him dragged out and beaten in the court hall, then condemned him to lifelong exile in Rangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，逃歸，為吏跡捕，流北庭。

translations.literal: After more than a year he fled back and was tracked down and seized by officials, then exiled to Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he fled back, was tracked down and seized, and was exiled to Beiting.

sentences.zh: 無復名檢，專居賄，五年至數千萬。

translations.literal: He no longer cared for reputation and devoted himself to bribery; within five years he amassed tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He cast off all regard for reputation and devoted himself to bribery. Within five years he amassed tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 娶降胡女為妻，妻有黃金、駿馬、牛羊，以財自雄。

translations.literal: He took a surrendered barbarian woman as wife. She had gold, fine horses, and cattle and sheep, and with her wealth he made himself a local power.
translations.idiomatic: He married a surrendered barbarian woman who possessed gold, fine horses, cattle, and sheep; with her wealth he made himself a local power.

sentences.zh: 養客數百人。

translations.literal: He kept several hundred retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He maintained several hundred clients.

sentences.zh: 自北庭屬京師，多其客，廞诇朝廷事，聞知十常七八。

translations.literal: From Beiting to the capital, many of his retainers spied on court affairs, and he learned seven or eight times out of ten what was happening.
translations.idiomatic: From Beiting down to the capital, many of his clients watched the court; seven or eight times in ten he knew what was afoot.

sentences.zh: 時補闕李秦授為武後謀曰：「讖言『代武者劉』，劉無強姓，殆流人乎？

translations.literal: At the time remonstrance supplement Li Qinshou plotted for Empress Wu and said, "A prophecy says, 'He who replaces Wu is Liu.' Among the strong surnamed Liu, perhaps it means an exile?
translations.idiomatic: At the time remonstrance supplement Li Qinshou plotted for Empress Wu and said, "A prophecy reads, 'He who replaces Wu is Liu.' Among powerful lines surnamed Liu, perhaps it means an exile?

sentences.zh: 今大臣流放者數萬族，使之葉亂，社稷憂也。」

translations.literal: Exiled great ministers now number tens of thousands of clans. If they are driven to disorder, the altars of state will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Exiled great ministers now number tens of thousands of clans. If they are driven to disorder, the altars of state will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 後謂然，夜拜秦授考功員外郎，分走使者，賜墨詔，尉安流人，實命殺之。

translations.literal: The empress thought this correct. That night she promoted Qinshou to outer court official of the Ministry of Personnel and sent envoys in all directions with sealed edicts to comfort the exiles—in fact ordering them killed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress agreed. That night she promoted Qinshou to outer court official of the Ministry of Personnel and sent envoys in all directions with sealed edicts to comfort the exiles—in fact ordering them killed.

sentences.zh: 伷先前知，以橐駝載金幣、賓客奔突厥。

translations.literal: Xianxian learned of this beforehand, loaded gold and coins on camels with his guests, and fled toward the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxian learned of it beforehand, loaded gold and coins onto camels with his guests, and fled toward the Turks.

sentences.zh: 行未遠，都護遣兵追之，與格鬥，為所執。

translations.literal: Before he had gone far, the protectorate sent troops in pursuit. They fought, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He had not gone far when the protectorate sent soldiers after him. After a fight, they seized him.

sentences.zh: 械系獄，以狀聞。

translations.literal: He was shackled and imprisoned, and the matter was reported.
translations.idiomatic: They put him in chains and prison and reported the case.

sentences.zh: 會武後度流人已誅，畏天下姍誚，更遣使者安撫十道，以好言自解釋曰：「前使使慰安有罪，而不曉朕意，擅誅殺，殘忍不道，朕甚自咎。

translations.literal: It happened that Empress Wu judged the exiles already executed and feared mockery throughout the realm. She sent envoys again to comfort the ten circuits, offering kind words in self-explanation: "The earlier envoys were sent to comfort the guilty, yet without understanding my intent they executed people on their own authority—cruel and contrary to the Way. I deeply reproach myself.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, judging the exiles already executed and fearing mockery throughout the realm, sent envoys again to comfort the ten circuits with kind words of self-explanation: "The earlier envoys were sent to comfort the guilty, yet without understanding my intent they executed people on their own authority—cruel and contrary to the Way. I deeply reproach myself.

sentences.zh: 今流人存者一切縱還。」

translations.literal: All exiles who still survive are now to be released and sent home."
translations.idiomatic: All exiles who still survive are now to be released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 繇是伷先得不死。

translations.literal: Thereby Xianxian was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xianxian was spared death.

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，求炎後，授先太子詹事丞。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, he sought Yan's descendants and appointed Xianxian vice director of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong regained the throne, he sought out Yan's heirs and made Xianxian vice director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 遷秦、桂、廣三州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand protector of Qin, Gui, and Guang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand protector of the Qin, Gui, and Guang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 坐累且誅，賴宰相張說右之，免官。

translations.literal: Implicated in a case and nearly executed, he was spared only because chancellor Zhang Yue supported him, and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in a case and nearly executed, he was spared only because chancellor Zhang Yue supported him and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 久乃擢范陽節度使，太原、京兆尹。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to military commissioner of Fanyang and concurrently mayor of Taiyuan and Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was promoted military commissioner of Fanyang and concurrently mayor of Taiyuan and Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 以京師官冗，奏罷畿縣員外及試官。

translations.literal: Because official posts in the capital were redundant, he memorialized to abolish supplemental and probationary posts in the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the capital overstaffed, he memorialized to abolish supplemental and probationary posts in the capital commanderies.

sentences.zh: 進工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of public works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 年八十六，以東京留守累封翼城縣公，卒官下。

translations.literal: At eighty-six, as eastern capital regent he was repeatedly enfeoffed Baron of Yicheng and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-six, as regent of the eastern capital he was repeatedly enfeoffed Baron of Yicheng and died in office.

sentences.zh: 劉祎之，字希美，常州晉陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi, courtesy name Ximei, was a native of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi, styled Ximei, came from Jinling in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父子翼，字小心，在隋為著作郎。

translations.literal: His father Ziyi, courtesy name Xiaoxin, served in Sui as director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziyi, styled Xiaoxin, served in Sui as director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 峭直有行，嘗面折僚友短，退無餘訾。

translations.literal: Steep, upright, and principled, he would openly reprove colleagues' faults to their faces, yet after retiring left no lingering complaint against him.
translations.idiomatic: Severe, upright, and principled, he would rebuke colleagues' faults to their faces, yet none lingered in resentment after he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李伯藥曰：「子翼詈人，人都不憾。」

translations.literal: Li Boyao said, "When Ziyi scolds people, they bear no resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Li Boyao said, "When Ziyi scolds people, they bear no resentment.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召之，辭以母老，詔許終養。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan period he was summoned, but declined on the grounds that his mother was old. An edict permitted him to remain and care for her to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan period he was summoned but declined because his mother was old. An edict permitted him to remain and care for her to the end.

sentences.zh: 江南道巡察使李襲譽嘉其孝，表所居為孝慈裏。

translations.literal: Jiangnan circuit inspection commissioner Li Xiyu praised his filial piety and memorialized that his neighborhood be named Filial and Kind Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan circuit inspector Li Xiyu praised his filial devotion and had his neighborhood named Filial and Kind Lane.

sentences.zh: 母已喪，召拜吳王府功曹參軍，終著作郎、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: After his mother died he was summoned and appointed aide to the Prince of Wu's household, and ended as director of the Imperial Library and direct scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he was summoned and appointed aide to the Prince of Wu's household, ending as director of the Imperial Library and direct scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 祎之少與孟利貞、高智周、郭正一俱以文辭稱，號「劉孟高郭」，並直昭文館。

translations.literal: In youth Yizhi, together with Meng Lizhen, Gao Zhizhou, and Guo Zhengyi, was famed for literary talent and was called "Liu, Meng, Gao, and Guo." All served as direct scholars of the Zhaowen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Yizhi, with Meng Lizhen, Gao Zhizhou, and Guo Zhengyi, won fame for elegant writing and was known as "Liu, Meng, Gao, and Guo." All served as direct scholars in the Zhaowen Academy.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右史、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to right historiographer and direct scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to right historiographer and direct scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 上元中，與元萬頃等偕召入禁中，論次新書凡千餘篇。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan period, together with Yuan Wanqing and others he was summoned into the inner palace and arranged more than a thousand new books.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan period, together with Yuan Wanqing and others, he was summoned into the inner palace and arranged more than a thousand new books.

sentences.zh: 高宗又密與參決時政，以分宰相權，時謂「北門學士」。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong also secretly had him join in deciding current policy to divide the chancellors' power. At the time they were called the "Northern Gate Academicians."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong also secretly brought him into deliberations on current policy to split the chancellors' power; at the time they were called the "Northern Gate Academicians."

sentences.zh: 兄懿之，亦給事中，同兩省。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yizhi the elder was also a supervising secretary; both served in the two departments.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yizhi the elder was also a supervising secretary; both held posts in the two departments.

sentences.zh: 先是，姊為內官，武後遣至外家問疾，祎之因賀蘭敏之私省之，坐流巂州。

translations.literal: Earlier, his elder sister had been an inner palace attendant. When Empress Wu sent her to her natal home to inquire after illness, Yizhi privately visited her through Helan Minzhi and was exiled to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his elder sister had served in the inner palace. When Empress Wu sent her to her natal home on a sick visit, Yizhi used Helan Minzhi to visit her in secret and was exiled to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 後為丐還，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later he begged to return and was appointed drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he begged permission to return and was appointed drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，吐蕃寇邊，帝訪侍臣所以置之、討之之宜，人人異謀，礻之獨勸帝：「夷狄猶禽獸，雖被馮陵，不足校，願戢威，紓百姓之急。」

translations.literal: In the Yifeng period, when Tibet raided the frontier, the emperor asked attendant ministers how to settle and suppress them. Each offered a different plan. Liu Yizhi alone urged the emperor, "Barbarians are like beasts. Though they have been insulted, it is not worth contending over. I wish you would sheathe your might and ease the people's distress."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng period, when Tibet raided the frontier, the emperor asked attendant ministers how to settle and suppress them. Each offered a different plan. Liu Yizhi alone urged the emperor, "Barbarians are like beasts. Though they have been insulted, it is not worth contending over. I wish you would sheathe your might and ease the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 帝內其言。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inwardly accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 俄拜相王府司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed marshal of the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named marshal of the Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 檢校中書侍郎，帝謂曰：「卿家忠孝，朕子賴卿以師矩，冀蓬在麻不扶而挺也。」

translations.literal: As acting vice minister of the Secretariat, the emperor said to him, "Your family is loyal and filial. My son relies on you as teacher and measure. I hope that like rushes among hemp he will stand straight without support."
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice minister of the Secretariat, the emperor told him, "Your house is known for loyalty and filial piety. My son depends on you as his teacher and measure. I hope that among hemp, like rushes, he will stand straight without being propped."

sentences.zh: 後既立王為帝，以其參奉大議，愈親之，擢中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，賜爵臨淮縣男。

translations.literal: After the empress had installed the prince as emperor, because he participated in great deliberations she grew ever closer to him, promoted him to vice minister of the Secretariat and one of the Three Chiefs of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and granted him the title Baron of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress enthroned the prince, she drew still closer to him for his part in weighty deliberations, promoted him to vice minister of the Secretariat and one of the Three Chiefs of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed him Baron of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 方是時，詔令叢繁，祎之思致華敏，裁可占授，少選可待也。

translations.literal: At that time edicts and orders were numerous and complex. Yizhi's thinking was refined and quick; he could draft and approve on the spot, and in a short while one could wait upon his completion.
translations.idiomatic: In those days edicts and orders piled up in profusion. Yizhi's mind was polished and quick: he could draft and approve on the spot, and in a little while one had only to wait for him to finish.

sentences.zh: 司門員外郎房先敏坐累貶衛州司馬，訴於相府，內史騫味道謂曰：「太后旨。」

translations.literal: Outer gate vice director Fang Xianmin, implicated in a case, was demoted marshal of Weizhou. He appealed at the chancellor's office. Inner scribe Qian Weidao said to him, "It is the empress dowager's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Outer gate vice director Fang Xianmin, implicated in a case, was demoted marshal of Weizhou. He appealed at the chancellor's office. Inner scribe Qian Weidao said to him, "It is the empress dowager's intent.

sentences.zh: 祎之曰：「乃上從有司所奏雲。」

translations.literal: Yizhi said, "It is simply that the sovereign followed what the department submitted."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi said, "It is simply that the sovereign followed what the department submitted."

sentences.zh: 後聞，以味道歸非於上，貶青州刺史，加祎之太中大夫，賜物百段。

translations.literal: When the empress heard this, she held that Weidao had shifted blame onto the sovereign, demoted him to prefect of Qingzhou, promoted Yizhi to grand master of the palace, and bestowed a hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard this, she held that Weidao had shifted blame onto the sovereign, demoted him to prefect of Qingzhou, promoted Yizhi to grand master of the palace, and bestowed a hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 後因曰：「君為元首，臣為股肱，以手足疾移於腹背，尚為一體乎？

translations.literal: Later she also said, "The ruler is the head; ministers are the arms and legs. If illness in the hands and feet moves to the belly and back, are they still one body?
translations.idiomatic: Later she also said, "The ruler is the head; ministers are the arms and legs. If illness in the hands and feet moves to the belly and back, are they still one body?

sentences.zh: 礻之引咎於已，忠臣也。」

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi took blame upon himself—he is a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi took the blame upon himself—a loyal minister indeed.

sentences.zh: 納言王德真推順曰：「戴至德無異才，惟能歸善於君，為時所服。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance officer Wang Dezhen deferentially said, "Dai Zhide had no extraordinary talent, yet he alone knew how to attribute good to the ruler, and the age respected him."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officer Wang Dezhen deferentially said, "Dai Zhide had no extraordinary talent, yet he alone knew how to attribute good to the ruler, and the age respected him."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 後私語鳳閣舍人賈大隱曰：「後能廢昏立明，盍反政以安天下？」

translations.literal: Later she privately said to Fengge drafting officer Jia Dayin, "The empress was able to depose the dim and establish the bright—why not return power to settle the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Later she privately said to Fengge drafting officer Jia Dayin, "The empress was able to depose the dim and establish the bright—why not return power to settle the realm?"

sentences.zh: 大隱表其言，後怒曰：「祎之乃負我！」

translations.literal: Dayin reported her words. The empress angrily said, "Yizhi has betrayed me!"
translations.idiomatic: Dayin reported her words. The empress angrily said, "Yizhi has betrayed me!"

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，或告祎之，受歸誠州都督孫萬榮金，與許敬宗妾私通，太后遣肅州刺史王本立鞫治，以敕示祎之，祎之曰：「不經鳳閣鸞臺，何謂之敕！」

translations.literal: In the Chuigong period someone reported that Yizhi had received gold from Sun Wanrong, military commissioner of Guicheng, and had a private affair with Xu Jingzong's concubine. The empress dowager sent Sizhou inspector Wang Benli to investigate. When the edict was shown to Yizhi, he said, "Without passing through Fengge and Luantai, how can this be called an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuigong period someone reported that Yizhi had received gold from Sun Wanrong, military commissioner of Guicheng, and had a private affair with Xu Jingzong's concubine. The empress dowager sent Sizhou inspector Wang Benli to investigate. When the edict was shown to Yizhi, he said, "Without passing through Fengge and Luantai, how can this be called an edict!"

sentences.zh: 後以為拒制使，賜死於家，年五十七。

translations.literal: The empress considered this refusal of the imperial commissioner and ordered him executed at home. He was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The empress considered this refusal of the imperial commissioner and ordered him executed at home. He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 初，祎之得罪，睿宗以舊屬申理之，姻友冀得釋。

translations.literal: When Yizhi first fell into guilt, Ruizong, as an old associate, pleaded on his behalf, and relatives and friends hoped he would be released.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi first fell afoul of the law, Ruizong, as an old associate, spoke in his defense, and kin and friends hoped he would be freed.

sentences.zh: 祎之曰：「吾死矣。

translations.literal: Yizhi said, "I am as good as dead.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi said, "I am already as good as dead.

sentences.zh: 太后威福由己，而帝營救，速吾禍也！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager holds power and favor in her own hands, yet the emperor tries to rescue me—that will hasten my ruin!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager holds power and favor in her own hands, yet the emperor tries to rescue me—that will hasten my ruin!

sentences.zh: 在獄上疏自陳。

translations.literal: In prison he submitted a memorial stating his case.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he submitted a memorial stating his case.

sentences.zh: 臨誅，洗沐，神色自若。

translations.literal: Facing execution, he washed and composed himself, his expression calm.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, he washed, composed himself, and looked untroubled.

sentences.zh: 命其子執筆占為表，子號塞不能書，祎之乃自捉筆，得數紙，詞懇哀到，人皆傷之。

translations.literal: He ordered his son to take brush and draft a memorial, but the son sobbed too hard to write. Yizhi then took the brush himself and wrote several sheets; the words were earnest and moving, and all who read them grieved.
translations.idiomatic: He told his son to take brush and draft a memorial, but the boy choked with sobs and could not write. Yizhi then took the brush himself and filled several sheets; the plea was sorrowful and sincere, and all who read it grieved.

sentences.zh: 麟臺郎郭翰、太子文學周思鈞悵嘆其文，後惡之，貶翰巫州司法參軍，思鈞播州司倉參軍。

translations.literal: Lin Tai Lang Guo Han and crown prince literary scholar Zhou Sijun lamented his writing. The empress hated this and demoted Han to judicial aide in Wuzhou and Sijun to secretary of the Si Cang section in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Tai Lang Guo Han and crown prince literary scholar Zhou Sijun mourned the quality of his writing. The empress resented this and demoted Han to judicial aide in Wuzhou and Sijun to secretary of the Si Cang section in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗嗣位，贈祎之中書令。

translations.literal: When Ruizong succeeded, Yizhi was posthumously made chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong succeeded to the throne, Yizhi was posthumously named chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 翰者，嘗為御史，巡察隴右。

translations.literal: Han had once served as censor and inspected Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Han had once served as censor, inspecting Longyou.

sentences.zh: 多所按劾。

translations.literal: He impeached many people.
translations.idiomatic: He brought many impeachments.

sentences.zh: 次寧州，時狄仁傑為刺史，民爭言有異政。

translations.literal: When he reached Ningzhou, Di Renjie was then prefect, and the people competed to speak of his unusual governance.
translations.idiomatic: When he stopped at Ningzhou, Di Renjie was then prefect, and the people all clamored to praise his unusual good governance.

sentences.zh: 翰就館，以筆紙置於案，謂僚屬曰：「入其境，其政可知，願薦使君美於朝，毋久留。」

translations.literal: Han went to the guest lodge, placed brush and paper on the desk, and said to his staff, "Entering this district, its governance can be known. I wish to recommend the prefect's excellence to the court—do not stay long."
translations.idiomatic: Han went to the guest lodge, placed brush and paper on the desk, and said to his staff, "Entering this district, its governance can be known. I wish to recommend the prefect's excellence to the court—do not stay long.

sentences.zh: 即命駕去。

translations.literal: He then ordered his carriage and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his carriage and departed.

sentences.zh: 性寬簡，讀《老子》至「和其光，同其塵」，慨然曰：「大雅君子，以保其身。」

translations.literal: By nature he was broad and simple. Reading the Laozi to the line "blend your light and be one with the dust," he sighed and said, "The great elegant gentleman preserves himself."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was broad and simple. Reading the Laozi to the line "blend your light and be one with the dust," he sighed and said, "The great elegant gentleman preserves himself."

sentences.zh: 乃辭憲官，改麟臺郎雲。

translations.literal: He then resigned his censorial post and changed to Lin Tai Lang.
translations.idiomatic: He then resigned his censorial post and changed to Lin Tai Lang.

sentences.zh: 方今人不加富、盜賊未衰、禮誼浸薄者，下吏不稱職，庶官非其才，取人之道有所未盡也。

translations.literal: At present the people do not grow richer, bandits have not declined, and ritual and righteousness grow ever thinner—because lower officials do not fit their posts, ordinary officials are not suited to their talents, and the way of selecting men has not yet been fully perfected.
translations.idiomatic: Today the people do not grow richer, bandits have not declined, and ritual and righteousness grow ever thinner—because lower officials fail their posts, ordinary officials lack the right talents, and the way of selecting men remains incomplete.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀，庶事草創，人物固乏。

translations.literal: In the Wude and Zhenguan periods, all affairs were newly established and talented men were indeed scarce.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude and Zhenguan periods, affairs were newly established and talented men were indeed scarce.

sentences.zh: 天祚大聖，享國永年，異人間出。

translations.literal: Heaven has blessed a great sage; the state enjoys long years, and extraordinary men appear one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has blessed us with a sage; the dynasty enjoys enduring years, and extraordinary men rise one after another.

sentences.zh: 諸色人流，歲以千計，官有常員，人無定限，選集猥至，十不收一，取舍淆紊。

translations.literal: Men of every sort pour in by the thousand each year. Offices have fixed quotas, yet men have no fixed limit. Candidates crowd the selection lists; fewer than one in ten is taken. Acceptance and rejection are confused and disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: Men of every sort pour in by the thousand each year. Offices have fixed quotas, yet candidates have no fixed limit. Selection lists overflow; fewer than one in ten is chosen. Acceptance and rejection fall into confusion.

sentences.zh: 夏、商以前，制度多闕。

translations.literal: Before Xia and Shang, institutions were largely lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xia and Shang, institutions were largely incomplete.

sentences.zh: 至周，煥然可觀。

translations.literal: By Zhou they shone brilliantly and could be clearly seen.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhou, they shone forth and could be admired.

sentences.zh: 諸侯之臣不皆命天子，王朝庶官不專一職。

translations.literal: The ministers of feudal lords were not all appointed by the Son of Heaven, and officials of the royal court did not each hold a single office.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords' ministers were not all appointed by the Son of Heaven, and royal court officials did not each hold a single post.

sentences.zh: 穆王以伯冏為太仆正，命曰：「慎簡乃僚。」

translations.literal: King Mu made Bo Jiong grand master of the Imperial Stud and commanded him, "Carefully choose your subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: King Mu made Bo Jiong grand master of the Imperial Stud and commanded him, "Carefully choose your subordinates.

sentences.zh: 此乃自擇下吏之言也。

translations.literal: This is language about choosing lower officials for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: This is language about choosing lower officials for oneself.

sentences.zh: 太仆正，特中大夫耳，尚以僚屬委之，則三公、九卿亦當然也。

translations.literal: The grand master of the Imperial Stud was only a grand master of the palace, yet even his subordinates were entrusted to him—how much more should the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers be the same.
translations.idiomatic: The grand master of the Imperial Stud was only a grand master of the palace, yet even his subordinates were entrusted to him—how much more, then, for the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 故太宰、內史並掌爵祿廢置，司徒、司馬別掌興賢詔事。

translations.literal: Therefore the grand minister and the inner scribe together managed enfeoffment, salary, dismissal, and appointment; the minister of education and the minister of war separately managed raising the worthy and issuing edicts on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the grand minister and inner scribe together handled enfeoffment, salary, dismissal, and appointment, while the minister of education and minister of war separately handled raising the worthy and issuing edicts.

sentences.zh: 是分任群司而統以數職，王命其大者，而自擇其小者。

translations.literal: This was to divide responsibility among the various offices and unify them under several posts: the king commanded the greater matters and chose the lesser ones himself.
translations.idiomatic: This divided responsibility among the offices under several posts: the king commanded great matters and chose lesser ones himself.

sentences.zh: 漢制，諸侯自置吏四百石以下，其傅、相大臣則漢為置之；

translations.literal: Under Han institutions, feudal lords themselves appointed officials below four hundred shi, while tutors, chancellors, and great ministers were appointed by Han;
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, feudal lords appointed their own officials below four hundred shi, while tutors, chancellors, and great ministers were appointed by the Han court;

sentences.zh: 州郡掾史、督郵、從事，悉任之牧守。

translations.literal: prefectural and district clerks, postal inspectors, and attendants were all entrusted to the governors and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: prefectural and district clerks, postal inspectors, and attendants were all left to governors and prefects.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉以後，始歸吏部，而迄於今。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, power returned to the Ministry of Personnel, and so it has remained to the present.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward it passed to the Ministry of Personnel, and so it has remained to this day.

sentences.zh: 以刀筆量才，簿書察行，法與世弊，其來久矣。

translations.literal: Measuring talent with the brush and examining conduct through ledgers—the law and the age decay together, and this has been so for long.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring talent with the brush and testing conduct through ledgers—law and age decay together; this has gone on for long.

sentences.zh: 尺丈之量，鍾庾之器，非所及則不能度，非所受則無以容，況天下之大、士類之眾，可委數人手乎！

translations.literal: The measure of foot and ten-foot rod, the vessel of bell and granary bin—what they cannot reach they cannot measure; what they cannot hold they cannot contain. How much more the vast realm and the multitude of scholars—can these be entrusted to the hands of a few men!
translations.idiomatic: A foot-rule and ten-foot rod, a bell measure and granary vessel—what they cannot reach they cannot measure, what they cannot hold they cannot contain. How much less can the vast realm and multitude of scholars be placed in a few men's hands!

sentences.zh: 又屍厥任者，間非其選，至為人擇官，為身擇利，下筆系親疏，措情觀勢要，悠悠風塵，此焉奔競，使百行折之一面，九能斷之數言，不亦難乎。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who occupy their posts in name alone are sometimes not the right choice. Some choose offices for others and choose profit for themselves; the brush ties itself to kin and distance, and feeling watches power and influence. Through drifting dust and wind they rush to compete here, making a hundred virtues fold into one face and nine abilities judged by a few words—is this not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who occupy their posts in name alone are sometimes not the right choice. Some choose offices for others and profit for themselves; the brush ties itself to kin and distance, and feeling watches power and influence. Through drifting dust and wind they rush to compete here, making a hundred virtues fold into one face and nine abilities judged by a few words—is this not difficult?

sentences.zh: 且臣聞蒞官者，不可以無學。

translations.literal: Moreover, your subject has heard that one who takes office cannot be without learning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have heard that one who holds office cannot do so without learning.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「學以從政，不聞以政入學。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Documents says, "Study in order to enter government; one does not hear of entering government in order to study."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Documents says, "Study in order to enter government; one does not hear of entering government in order to study.

sentences.zh: 今貴戚子弟一皆早仕，弘文、崇賢、千牛、輦腳之類，程較既淺，技能亦薄，而門閥有素，資望自高。

translations.literal: Now sons of noble houses all enter office early. For Hongwen, Chongxian, Thousand-Ox, and Palace Escort posts, their training is shallow and their skills meager, yet their gates and clans have long standing and their prestige is naturally high.
translations.idiomatic: Now sons of noble houses all enter office early. For Hongwen, Chongxian, Thousand-Ox, and Palace Escort posts, their training is shallow and their skills meager, yet their gates and clans have long standing and their prestige is naturally high.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂胄子者，必裁諸學，少則受業，長而入官，然後移家事國，謂之德進。

translations.literal: What are called scions must be tested through study: in youth they receive instruction; when grown they enter office—only then do they shift family affairs to state affairs. This is called advancing through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: What are called scions must be shaped through study: taught in youth, entering office when grown—only then do they turn from family to state. That is advancing through virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫少仕則不務學，輕試則無才。

translations.literal: Entering office young, one does not pursue study; lightly tested, one lacks talent.
translations.idiomatic: Enter office too young and one neglects study; tested too lightly and one lacks ability.

sentences.zh: 又勛官、三衛、流外之屬，不待州縣之舉，直取書判，非先德後言之誼。

translations.literal: Also merit officials, Three Guards, and outer-stream posts do not await recommendation from prefectures and districts but are taken directly by document judgment—not the principle of virtue first and words after.
translations.idiomatic: Merit officials, Three Guards, and outer-stream ranks do not wait for prefectural recommendation but enter directly by document judgment—not putting virtue before words.

sentences.zh: 臣聞國之用人，如人用財，貧者止糟糠，富者餘粱肉。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in using men a state is like a man using wealth: the poor stop at chaff and husks; the rich have grain and meat to spare.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state using men is like a man using wealth: the poor make do with chaff; the rich have grain and meat to spare.

sentences.zh: 故當衰弊之乏，則磨策朽鈍以馭之；

translations.literal: Therefore when decline and exhaustion prevail, one uses worn whips and blunt blades to drive men on;
translations.idiomatic: When decline and want prevail, one drives men with worn whips and blunt blades;

sentences.zh: 太平多士，則遴柬髦俊而使之。

translations.literal: when peace brings many scholars, one carefully selects the finest and sends them forth.
translations.idiomatic: In times of peace, when scholars abound, one picks out the outstanding and puts them to use.

sentences.zh: 今選者猥多，宜以簡練為急。

translations.literal: Now candidates are too many; selection and refinement should be urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates are now too many; selection and refinement must be urgent.

sentences.zh: 竊見制書，三品至九品並得薦士，此誠仄席旁求意也。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen edicts allowing ranks from third to ninth to recommend scholars. This truly expresses the intent of leaving one's seat and seeking widely.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen edicts allowing ranks from third to ninth to recommend scholars—truly the spirit of rising from one's seat to seek widely.

sentences.zh: 但褒貶不明，故上不憂黜責，下不盡搜揚，莫慎所舉，而茍以應命。

translations.literal: But praise and blame are unclear, so superiors do not fear demotion and censure, and inferiors do not fully search and promote. None carefully considers whom they recommend, but merely responds to the command.
translations.idiomatic: But praise and blame are unclear, so superiors do not fear demotion and inferiors do not fully search and promote. None carefully weighs whom they recommend, but merely answers the command.

sentences.zh: 且惟賢知賢，聖人篤論。

translations.literal: Moreover, only the worthy know the worthy—the sages spoke firmly on this.
translations.idiomatic: Only the worthy know the worthy—the sages insisted on this.

sentences.zh: 臯陶既舉，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Once Gao Yao had made his selections, the unkind stood far off.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Yao had chosen, the unkind stood far away.

sentences.zh: 身茍濫進，庸及知人？

translations.literal: If one recklessly advances oneself, how can one reach knowing others?
translations.idiomatic: If one advances recklessly oneself, how can one know others?

sentences.zh: 不擇舉者之緊，而責所舉之濫，不可得已。

translations.literal: If one does not tighten the strictness of those who recommend and yet demands that those recommended not be reckless, that cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Without tightening standards on those who recommend, yet demanding that the recommended not be reckless—that cannot be achieved.

sentences.zh: 以陛下聖明，國家德業，而不建經久之策，但顧望魏、晉遺風，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely clarity and the state's virtue and achievement, yet not establishing a long-lasting policy but only looking back to the surviving customs of Wei and Jin—your subject is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's sagely clarity and the state's virtue and achievement, yet no lasting policy is built, only looking back to Wei and Jin survivals—I am privately baffled.

sentences.zh: 願少遵周、漢之規，以分吏部選，即所用詳，所失鮮矣。

translations.literal: I wish you would slightly follow the rules of Zhou and Han, divide the Ministry of Personnel's selections, and then those used will be carefully chosen and those missed will be few.
translations.idiomatic: I wish you would follow Zhou and Han precedents in part, divide the Ministry of Personnel's selections—and then what is chosen will be careful and what is missed will be few.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 進拜文昌左丞、鸞臺侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left director of the Wenchang Department, Luantai vice minister, and one of the Three Chiefs of Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted left director of Wenchang, Luantai vice minister, and one of the Three Chiefs of Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 遷地官尚書，檢校納言。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the terrestrial department and made acting remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to minister of the terrestrial department and concurrently served as acting remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 玄同與裴炎締交，能保終始，故號「耐久朋」。

translations.literal: Xuantong formed a friendship with Pei Yan and preserved it to the end; therefore they were called "long-lasting friends."
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong and Pei Yan made a friendship that endured to the end; they were called "long-lasting friends."

sentences.zh: 先是，狄仁傑督太原運，失米萬斛，將坐誅，玄同救免。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Di Renjie supervised transport at Taiyuan and lost ten thousand dan of grain, he was about to be punished with death. Xuantong saved him and had him spared.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Di Renjie supervised grain transport at Taiyuan and lost ten thousand dan, he faced execution. Xuantong intervened and had him spared.

sentences.zh: 而河陽令周興未知也，數於朝堂聽命。

translations.literal: Yet Heyang magistrate Zhou Xing did not know this and repeatedly waited for orders in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang magistrate Zhou Xing did not know this and repeatedly waited for orders in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 玄同曰：「明府可去矣，毋久留。」

translations.literal: Xuantong said, "Magistrate, you may go—do not stay long."
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong said, "Magistrate, you may go—do not stay long.

sentences.zh: 興以為沮己，銜之，至是誣玄同言「太后老矣，當復皇嗣」。

translations.literal: Xing thought this obstructed him and resented it. At this time he falsely accused Xuantong of saying, "The empress dowager is old and should restore the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xing thought this obstructed him and resented it. At this time he falsely accused Xuantong of saying, "The empress dowager is old and should restore the imperial heir."

sentences.zh: 後不察，賜死於家，年七十三。

translations.literal: The empress did not examine the matter and ordered him executed at home. He was seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: The empress did not investigate and ordered him executed at home. He was seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 初，監察御史房濟監刑，謂曰：「丈人盍上變？

translations.literal: Earlier, when surveillance censor Fang Ji supervised the execution, he said, "Elder, why not submit a petition of grievance?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when surveillance censor Fang Ji supervised the execution, he said, "Elder, why not submit a petition of grievance?

sentences.zh: 冀召見，得自陳。」

translations.literal: Perhaps you would be summoned and could state your case yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps you would be summoned and could state your case yourself.

sentences.zh: 玄同曰：「人殺與鬼殺等耳，不能為告事人！」

translations.literal: Xuantong said, "Being killed by men and being killed by ghosts are the same—I cannot become an informer!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong said, "Being killed by men and being killed by ghosts are the same—I cannot become an informer!"

sentences.zh: 玄同子恬，字安禮，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xuantong's son Tian, courtesy name Anli, was famed for filial service to his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong's son Tian, styled Anli, was famed for filial service to his parents.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為御史主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and became chief clerk of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 開元中。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 至潁王傅。

translations.literal: He reached tutor of the Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to tutor of the Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 李昭德，雍州長安人。

translations.literal: Li Zhaode was a native of Chang'an in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaode came from Chang'an in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父乾祐，貞觀初為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Qianyou, in the early Zhenguan period, was palace attendant of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianyou served as palace attendant of the Department of State Affairs from the early Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 鄃令裴仁軌私役門卒，太宗欲斬之，乾祐曰：「法令與天下共之，非陛下獨有也。

translations.literal: Magistrate Pei Rengui of Yu privately used gate soldiers for labor. Emperor Taizong wished to execute him. Qianyou said, "Law and command are shared with the realm—they are not the sovereign's alone.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Pei Rengui of Yu privately used gate soldiers for labor. Emperor Taizong wished to execute him. Qianyou said, "Law and command belong to the realm together—they are not the sovereign's alone.

sentences.zh: 仁軌以輕罪致極刑，非畫一之制。

translations.literal: For Rengui's light offense to receive extreme punishment is not a uniform system.
translations.idiomatic: For a light offense Rengui would receive the utmost penalty—that is not one uniform standard.

sentences.zh: 刑罰不中，則民無所措手足。」

translations.literal: If punishments are not centered, then the people have nowhere to put hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: When punishments miss the mark, the people do not know where to stand.

sentences.zh: 帝意解，繇是免死。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind eased, and thereby Rengui was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind eased, and thereby Rengui was spared death.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Transfer: attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 母卒，廬墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When his mother died he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth until the mound was formed.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth until the mound was complete.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使就吊，表異其閭。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to offer condolences and marked his lane as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to condole and marked his lane as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 歷治書侍御史，有能名。

translations.literal: He served successively as attendant censor of judicial matters and was famed for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as attendant censor of judicial matters and won a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，擢御史大夫，為褚遂良所惡，出為邢、魏二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghui period he was promoted to censor-in-chief, but was disliked by Chu Suiliang and was sent out as prefect of Xing and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yonghui period he was promoted censor-in-chief, but Chu Suiliang disliked him and he was sent out as prefect of Xing and Wei.

sentences.zh: 乾祐雖強直，而昵小人。

translations.literal: Although Qianyou was forceful and upright, he was intimate with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Though Qianyou was forceful and upright, he was close to petty men.

sentences.zh: 嘗為書與所善吏，刺取朝廷事，迷隱其辭，為吏所賣，遂良白髮於朝，坐流州。

translations.literal: He once wrote a letter to a clerk he favored, probing court affairs with hidden wording, and was betrayed by the clerk. Suiliang reported it at court, and he was exiled to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a favored clerk, probing court affairs in hidden wording; the clerk betrayed him. Suiliang reported it at court, and he was exiled to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 臺拜滄州刺史。

translations.literal: The censorate appointed him prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate named him prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為司刑太常伯，舉雍州司功參軍崔擢為尚書郎，不得報，私語擢所以然。

translations.literal: He entered office as grand minister of justice and grand minister of imperial worship, recommended Yongzhou secretary Cui Zhuo for appointment as director of a ministry, received no reply, and privately told Zhuo why.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as grand minister of justice and imperial worship, recommended Yongzhou secretary Cui Zhuo for a ministry post, received no reply, and privately told Zhuo why.

sentences.zh: 後擢犯罪，告乾祐漏禁中語以自贖，詔免官，卒。

translations.literal: Later Zhuo committed a crime, reported Qianyou leaking inner-palace words to redeem himself; edict dismissed from office; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhuo ran afoul of the law, he claimed Qianyou had leaked palace secrets to save himself. An edict stripped Qianyou of office, and he died.

sentences.zh: 昭德強幹有父風，擢明經，累官御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zhaode was forceful and capable with his father's style. He passed the Mingjing examination and rose through offices to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode was forceful and capable in his father's mold. He passed the Mingjing examination and rose to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，坐事貶振州陵水尉。

translations.literal: In the early Yongchang period, implicated in an affair, he was demoted to magistrate of Lingshui in Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongchang era he was punished for an offense and demoted to magistrate of Lingshui in Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 還為夏官侍郎。

translations.literal: On return: vice minister of the summer department.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he became vice minister of the summer department.

sentences.zh: 如意元年，拜鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: First year of Ruyi, appointed Fengge vice minister, co-equal with Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ruyi he joined the council as Fengge vice minister, co-equal with Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 武後營神都，昭德規創文昌臺及定鼎、上東諸門，標置華壯。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu built the divine capital, Zhaode planned and created the Wenchang Platform and the Dingding, Shangdong, and other gates, marking them out in splendid grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu built the divine capital, Zhaode planned the Wenchang Platform and the Dingding, Shangdong, and other gates, marking them in splendid grandeur.

sentences.zh: 洛有二橋，司農卿韋機徙其一直長夏門，民利之，其一橋廢，省巨萬計。

translations.literal: Luoyang had two bridges. Minister of agriculture Wei Ji moved one straight to Changxia Gate to the people's benefit; the other bridge was abandoned, saving tens of millions in cost.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had two bridges. Minister of agriculture Wei Ji moved one straight to Changxia Gate to the people's benefit; the other was abandoned, saving tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 然洛水歲淙嚙之，繕者告勞。

translations.literal: Yet the Luo River gnawed at them year by year, and those who repaired them complained of exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Luo gnawed at them year by year, and those who repaired them complained of exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 昭德始累石代柱，銳其前，廝殺暴濤，水不能怒，自是無患。

translations.literal: Zhaode first piled stones in place of pillars and sharpened their fronts to cut the violent surges, so the water could not rage, and thereafter there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode first piled stones in place of pillars and sharpened their fronts to cut the violent surges, so the water could not rage—and thereafter there was no trouble.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校內史。

translations.literal: Soon: acting inner scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting inner scribe.

sentences.zh: 薛懷義討突厥，以昭德為行軍長史，不見虜還。

translations.literal: When Xue Huaiyi campaigned against the Turks, Zhaode served as chief of staff on the campaign and returned without encountering the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Huaiyi campaigned against the Turks, Zhaode served as chief of staff and returned without meeting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣任文昌左相，昭德諫曰：「承嗣已王，不宜典機衡，以惑眾庶。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi held the post of left director of Wenchang. Zhaode remonstrated, "Chengsi is already ennobled as king and should not manage the pivot of state, lest he mislead the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi held the post of left director of Wenchang. Zhaode remonstrated, "Chengsi is already ennobled as king and should not manage the pivot of state, lest he mislead the multitude.

sentences.zh: 且父子猶相篡奪，況姑侄乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, even father and son still usurp and seize from one another—how much more aunt and nephew?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even father and son still usurp and seize from one another—how much more aunt and nephew?

sentences.zh: 後矍然曰：「我未之思也。」

translations.literal: The empress started and said, "I had not thought of that."
translations.idiomatic: The empress started and said, "I had not thought of that."

sentences.zh: 乃罷承嗣為太子少保。

translations.literal: Chengsi was then removed as grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was then removed as grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 洛陽人王慶之率險佞數百人請以承嗣為皇太子，後不許；

translations.literal: A man of Luoyang, Wang Qingzhi, led several hundred crafty sycophants to request that Chengsi be made crown prince. The empress did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qingzhi of Luoyang led several hundred crafty sycophants to ask that Chengsi be made crown prince. The empress did not permit it;

sentences.zh: 固請，後遣昭德詰其故。

translations.literal: They pressed firmly; the empress sent Zhaode to question the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed hard, the empress dispatched Zhaode to demand their reasons.

sentences.zh: 昭德笞殺慶之，餘黨散走。

translations.literal: Zhaode flogged and killed Qingzhi; the remainder of the party scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode had Qingzhi beaten to death, and his followers fled in all directions.

sentences.zh: 因奏曰：「自古有侄為天子而為姑立廟乎？

translations.literal: He then memorialized, "Since antiquity has there ever been a nephew who became Son of Heaven and yet set up temples for his aunt?
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized, "Since antiquity has there ever been a nephew who became Son of Heaven and yet set up temples for his aunt?

sentences.zh: 以親親言之，天皇，陛下夫也；

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of kinship, the Heavenly Emperor was Your Majesty's husband;
translations.idiomatic: In terms of kinship, the Heavenly Emperor was Your Majesty's husband;

sentences.zh: 皇嗣，陛下子也。

translations.literal: The imperial heir is Your Majesty's son.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is your son.

sentences.zh: 當傳之子孫為萬世計。

translations.literal: Power should pass to son and grandson as a plan for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Power should pass to sons and grandsons as a plan for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 陛下承天皇顧托而有天下，又立承嗣，臣見天皇不來食矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the Heavenly Emperor's dying charge and gained the realm, yet if you establish Chengsi, I see the Heavenly Emperor will not come to receive offerings."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the Heavenly Emperor's dying charge and gained the realm—yet if you establish Chengsi, I see the Heavenly Emperor will not come to receive offerings.

sentences.zh: 后乃止。

translations.literal: The empress then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then stopped.

sentences.zh: 承嗣恨，譖短之。

translations.literal: Chengsi resented it and slandered him with short words.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi bore a grudge and spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「吾任昭德而獲安枕，是代我勞，非而所知也。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "I entrust myself to Zhaode and gain peaceful sleep—he takes my labor on himself. This is not something you understand.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I entrust myself to Zhaode and gain peaceful sleep—he takes my labor on himself. This is not something you understand.

sentences.zh: 有人獲洛水白石而赤文者，獻闕下曰：「此石赤心，故以獻。」

translations.literal: Someone obtained a white stone from the Luo River with red markings and presented it at court, saying, "This stone has a red heart, therefore it is offered."
translations.idiomatic: Someone obtained a white stone from the Luo River with red markings and presented it at court, saying, "This stone has a red heart, therefore it is offered."

sentences.zh: 昭德叱曰：「洛水余石豈盡能反邪？」

translations.literal: Zhaode rebuked him, "Are all the leftover stones of the Luo River able to turn over?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode rebuked him, "Are all the leftover stones of the Luo River able to turn over?"

sentences.zh: 時來俊臣、侯思止舞文法，數誅陷大臣，人皆懾懼。

translations.literal: At the time Lai Jun Chen and Hou Sizhi twisted the law with florid wording and repeatedly framed and destroyed great ministers, and all men feared them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lai Jun Chen and Hou Sizhi twisted the law with florid wording and repeatedly framed and destroyed great ministers, and all men feared them.

sentences.zh: 昭德每奏其誣罔不道狀，卒榜殺思止，其黨稍摧沮。

translations.literal: Zhaode repeatedly memorialized their false and unfilial conduct, and in the end had Sizhi beaten to death. Their faction gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode repeatedly memorialized their false and unfilial conduct and in the end had Sizhi beaten to death; their faction gradually weakened.

sentences.zh: 然昭德頗怙權，為眾指目。

translations.literal: Yet Zhaode relied heavily on power and became the target of many eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhaode leaned heavily on power and became the target of many eyes.

sentences.zh: 魯王府功曹參軍丘愔上疏曰：「臣聞魏冉誅庶族以安秦，忠也。

translations.literal: Qiu Yin, aide to the Prince of Lu's household, submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that Wei Ran executed the collateral clan to settle Qin—that was loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yin, aide to the Prince of Lu's household, submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that Wei Ran executed the collateral clan to settle Qin—that was loyalty.

sentences.zh: 弱諸侯以強國，功也；

translations.literal: weakening the feudal lords to strengthen the state—that was merit;
translations.idiomatic: Crippling the feudal lords to make the state strong—that too was merit;

sentences.zh: 然出入自專，擊斷無忌，威震人主，不聞有王，張祿一言而卒用憂死。

translations.literal: yet going in and out on his own authority, striking and judging without restraint, his authority shaking the ruler, with no king heard of—Zhang Lu with one word was finally used and died in worry.
translations.idiomatic: yet going in and out on his own authority, striking and judging without restraint, his authority shaking the ruler till no king was heard of—Zhang Lu with one word was finally employed and died in worry.

sentences.zh: 向使昭王不即覺悟，則秦之霸業或不傳子孫。

translations.literal: If King Zhao of Qin had not immediately awakened, then Qin's hegemony might not have passed to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Had King Zhao of Qin not woken at once, Qin's dominion might never have reached his heirs.

sentences.zh: 陛下天授以前，萬機獨斷，公卿百執具職而已。

translations.literal: Before Your Majesty received Heaven's mandate, the myriad affairs were decided alone; dukes, ministers, and the hundred offices merely filled their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before you received Heaven's mandate, you alone ruled; the great ministers and hundred offices simply did their jobs.

sentences.zh: 自長壽以來，厭怠細政，擢委昭德，乘總權綱，而才小任重，負氣強愎，聾盲下民，芻狗同列，刻薄慶賞，多所矯虔，聲威翕習，天下杜口。

translations.literal: Since the Changshou period you have grown weary of minute governance, elevated and entrusted Zhaode, seized the full reins of power—yet his talent was small and his burden heavy, his spirit proud and obstinate, deaf and blind to the people below, treating colleagues like straw dogs, harsh in rewards and punishments, correcting many matters, his authority gathering and learning, the realm silenced.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Changshou period you have grown weary of minute governance, elevated and entrusted Zhaode, and seized the full reins—yet his talent was small and his burden heavy, proud and obstinate, deaf to the people below, treating colleagues like straw dogs, harsh in rewards and punishments, correcting many matters until his authority gathered and the realm fell silent.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見南臺敕目，群臣奏請，陛下制已曰『可』，而昭德建言不可，制又從之。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen in the Southern Censorate's edict items that when ministers memorialized requests and Your Majesty's decision already read "approved," Zhaode argued it should not be so and the decision then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen in the Southern Censorate's edict items that when ministers memorialized and Your Majesty's decision already read 'approved,' Zhaode argued it should not be so and the decision then followed him.

sentences.zh: 且人臣參奉機密，獻可替否，事或便利，不豫咨謀，而畫可已行，方興駁異，是揚露擅命，以示於人，歸美引咎，誼不類此，一切奏讞，皆承風指，陰相傅會。

translations.literal: Moreover, when ministers participate in secrets and offer approval or rejection, if a matter is convenient they should consult beforehand; yet when approval is already marked and underway, he then raises objections—this exposes unauthorized command to show others, attributing beauty and drawing blame—right principle is not like this. All memorials and judgments follow the wind of his finger, secretly echoing one another.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers share secrets and offer approval or rejection, convenient matters should be consulted beforehand; yet when approval is already marked and underway, he raises objections—exposing unauthorized command to the world. The principle of attributing beauty and drawing blame is not like this. All memorials and judgments follow the wind of his finger, secretly echoing one another.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其膽，乃大於身，鼻息所沖，上拂雲漢。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that his gall is greater than his body, and the breath of his nostrils strikes up to the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that his gall is larger than his body, and the breath of his nostrils strikes up to the Milky Way.

sentences.zh: 夫小家治生，有千百之貲，將以托人，尚憂失授，況天下之重，可輕委寄乎？

translations.literal: In a small household managing livelihood, if one has a thousand or hundred in assets and wishes to entrust them to another, one still fears misplacing the trust—how much more the weight of the realm: can it be lightly entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: In a small household managing livelihood, if one has a thousand or hundred in assets and wishes to entrust them to another, one still fears misplacing trust—how much more the weight of the realm?

sentences.zh: 履霜堅冰，須防其漸。

translations.literal: Tread on frost and solid ice follows; one must guard against the gradual.
translations.idiomatic: Step on frost and frozen ground comes after—you must stop things at the beginning.

sentences.zh: 大權一去，收之良難。

translations.literal: Great power once lost—taking it back is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: Once authority slips away, it is hard to gather it back.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察臣之言。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to examine your subject's words."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to examine your subject's words.

sentences.zh: 又果毅鄧註著《石論》數千言，述其專恣，鳳閣舍人逄弘敏以聞。

translations.literal: Also resolute Deng Zhu wrote the "Stone Discourse" in several thousand words, describing his arbitrary willfulness, and Fengge drafting officer Pang Hongmin reported it.
