translations.idiomatic: Also resolute Deng Zhu wrote the "Stone Discourse" in several thousand words, describing his arbitrary willfulness, and Fengge drafting officer Pang Hongmin reported it.

sentences.zh: 後由是惡之，謂姚璹曰：「誠如所言，昭德固負國矣！」

translations.literal: The empress therefore hated him and said to Yao Shu, "If it is truly as they say, then Zhaode has indeed betrayed the state!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress therefore hated him and said to Yao Shu, "If it is truly as they say, then Zhaode has indeed betrayed the state!

sentences.zh: 乃貶欽州南賓尉。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to magistrate of Nanbin in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then demoted to magistrate of Nanbin in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄召授監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon summoned and appointed surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was recalled and made surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天二年，來俊臣誣以逆謀，既而俊臣亦下獄，同日誅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian, Lai Jun Chen falsely accused him of treasonous plotting. Soon Jun Chen also entered prison, and on the same day both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian, Lai Jun Chen falsely accused him of treason. Soon Jun Chen also entered prison, and on the same day both were executed.

sentences.zh: 時甚雨，眾庶莫不冤昭德而快俊臣。

translations.literal: At the time rain was heavy; the multitude all thought Zhaode wronged and rejoiced at Jun Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Rain poured that day, and common opinion held that Zhaode had been wronged and Jun Chen justly punished.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，贈左御史大夫。

translations.literal: Second year of Shenlong, posthumously granted left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenlong he was posthumously named left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，加贈司空。

translations.literal: Third year of Jianzhong, additionally posthumously granted minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong he received a further posthumous promotion to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 吉頊，洛州河南人。

translations.literal: Ji Xu was a native of Henan in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xu came from Henan in Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，性陰克，敢言事。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet tall, was by nature dark and harsh, and dared to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, was dark and harsh by nature, and dared speak on affairs.

sentences.zh: 舉進士及第。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination and received degree.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi examination and passed.

sentences.zh: 調明堂尉。

translations.literal: Assigned: magistrate of Mingtang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Mingtang.

sentences.zh: 父哲為易州刺史，坐賕當死，頊往見武承嗣，自陳有二女弟，請侍王巾盥者。

translations.literal: His father Zhe served as prefect of Yizhou and, implicated in bribery, was to be executed. Xu went to see Wu Chengsi and stated that he had two younger sisters and asked to serve the prince at towel and basin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhe served as prefect of Yizhou and, implicated in bribery, faced death. Xu went to see Wu Chengsi and said he had two younger sisters and asked to serve the prince at towel and basin.

sentences.zh: 承嗣喜，以犢車迎之。

translations.literal: Chengsi was pleased and with a calf cart welcomed them.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Chengsi sent an ox cart to fetch them.

sentences.zh: 三日未言，問其故，答曰：「父犯法且死，故憂之。」

translations.literal: For three days they did not speak. When asked the reason, they answered, "Our father violated the law and is about to die, therefore we grieve."
translations.idiomatic: For three days they did not speak. When asked the reason, they answered, "Our father violated the law and is about to die, therefore we grieve.

sentences.zh: 承嗣為表貸哲死，遷頊龍為監。

translations.literal: Chengsi submitted a memorial to spare Zhe from death and transferred Xu to supervisor of the imperial dragon stables.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi submitted a memorial to spare Zhe from death and transferred Xu to supervisor of the imperial dragon stables.

sentences.zh: 劉思禮謀反，頊上變事，後命武懿宗雜訊，因諷囚引近臣高閥生平所牾者凡三十六姓，捕系詔獄，搒楚百慘，以成其獄，同日論死，天下冤之。

translations.literal: When Liu Sil's plot at rebellion was reported by Xu in a petition of grievance, the empress ordered Wu Yizong to examine the case in mixed interrogation. Through prompting prisoners he implicated all thirty-six clans among close ministers whom Gao Que had opposed in life, seized them in the imperial prison, tortured them with a hundred cruel torments, and completed the case. On the same day they were sentenced to death, and the realm thought it a miscarriage of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Sil's plot was reported by Xu in a petition of grievance, the empress ordered Wu Yizong to examine the case in mixed interrogation. Through prompting prisoners he implicated all thirty-six clans among close ministers whom Gao Que had opposed in life, seized them in the imperial prison, tortured them with a hundred cruel torments, and completed the case. On the same day they were sentenced to death, and the realm thought it a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 擢右肅政臺中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the right Sucheng Platform.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted director of the right Sucheng Platform.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣下獄，司刑當以死，狀三日不下。

translations.literal: When Lai Jun Chen entered prison, the Ministry of Justice judged that he should die, yet the report was not issued for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Jun Chen entered prison, the Ministry of Justice judged death, yet the report was not issued for three days.

sentences.zh: 頊從武後遊苑中，因間言：「臣為陛下耳目，知俊臣狀入不出，人以為疑。」

translations.literal: Xu followed Empress Wu touring the garden and interposed, "Your subject serves Your Majesty as eyes and ears and knows Jun Chen's report has gone in but not come out. People think this suspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Xu followed Empress Wu touring the garden and interposed, "Your subject serves Your Majesty as eyes and ears and knows Jun Chen's report has gone in but not come out. People think this suspicious.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「朕以俊臣有功，徐思之。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "I consider Jun Chen has merit and will think on it slowly."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I consider Jun Chen has merit and will think on it slowly."

sentences.zh: 頊曰：「於安遠告虺貞反，今為成州司馬。

translations.literal: Xu said, "Yu Anyuan reported Hui Zhen's rebellion and now serves as marshal of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Yu Anyuan reported Hui Zhen's rebellion and now serves as marshal of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊臣誣殺忠良，罪惡如山，國蝥賊也，尚何惜？」

translations.literal: Jun Chen falsely killed the loyal and good; his crimes pile like mountains. He is a locust of the state—why still spare him?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun Chen falsely killed the loyal and good; his crimes pile like mountains. He is a locust of the state—why still spare him?

sentences.zh: 於是後斬俊臣，而召安遠為尚食奉禦。

translations.literal: Thereupon the empress executed Jun Chen and summoned Anyuan to be director of imperial food service.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the empress executed Jun Chen and summoned Anyuan to be director of imperial food service.

sentences.zh: 突厥陷趙、定，授檢校相州刺史，且募兵制虜南向。

translations.literal: Turks captured Zhao and Ding; granted acting prefect of Xiangzhou, and also to recruit troops to check the barbarians' southward movement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks took Zhao and Ding, he was named acting prefect of Xiangzhou and told to raise troops to block the enemy's march south.

sentences.zh: 頊辭不知武，後曰：「賊方走，藉卿坐鎮耳。」

translations.literal: Xu declined on the grounds that he did not know military affairs. The empress said, "The bandits are already fleeing—I borrow you to sit and hold the place."
translations.idiomatic: Xu declined on the grounds that he did not know military affairs. The empress said, "The bandits are already fleeing—I borrow you to sit and hold the place.

sentences.zh: 初，太原溫彬茂死高宗時，封一笥書，諉妻曰：「吾死後，須年及垂拱獻之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen Binmao of Taiyuan died in Emperor Gaozong's time, he sealed a box of writings and entrusted it to his wife, saying, "After my death, wait until the year reaches Chuigong and then present it."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wen Binmao of Taiyuan died in Emperor Gaozong's time, he sealed a box of writings and entrusted it to his wife, saying, "After my death, wait until the year reaches Chuigong and then present it."

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，妻上其書，言後革命事及突厥至趙去，故後知虜且還。

translations.literal: In the early Chuigong period his wife presented the book, which spoke of the empress's revolution and the Turks reaching Zhao and departing—therefore the empress knew the barbarians would return.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chuigong period his wife presented the book, which spoke of the empress's revolution and the Turks reaching Zhao and departing—therefore the empress knew the barbarians would return.

sentences.zh: 頊至，募士無應者，俄詔以皇太子為元帥，應募日數千。

translations.literal: Xu arrived; recruiting warriors, none responded; soon edict made crown prince commander-in-chief; recruits by the thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu got there, no one answered his call for men. Then the crown prince was made commander-in-chief by edict, and thousands enlisted each day.

sentences.zh: 頊還言狀，後曰：「人心若是耶？

translations.literal: Xu returned and reported the situation. The empress said, "Is the people's heart really like this?
translations.idiomatic: Xu returned and reported the situation. The empress said, "Is the people's heart really like this?

sentences.zh: 卿可為群臣道之。」

translations.literal: You may tell the ministers this."
translations.idiomatic: You may tell the ministers this.

sentences.zh: 頊誦語於朝，諸武惡之。

translations.literal: Xu recited the words at court, and the Wu clan hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu recited the words at court, and the Wu clan hated him.

sentences.zh: 始，頊善張易之、殿中少監田歸道、鳳閣舍人薛稷、正諫大夫員半千、夏官侍郎李迥秀，皆為控鶴內供奉。

translations.literal: At first Xu was friendly with Zhang Yizhi, Tian Guidao director of palace attendants, Xue Ji Fengge drafting officer, Yuan Banqian remonstrance grandee, Li Huixiu summer department vice minister—all Crane-Control inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu stood close to Zhang Yizhi, Tian Guidao, Xue Ji, Yuan Banqian, and Li Huixiu, all of them inner attendants of the Crane-Control Office.

sentences.zh: 頊又強敏，故後倚為腹心。

translations.literal: Xu again was forceful and sharp; therefore the empress relied on him as trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and quick-witted, Xu became one the empress trusted above all others.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年，進天官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenglì he was promoted to vice minister of the celestial department and co-equal with Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengli he was promoted vice minister of the celestial department and co-equal with Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 為刺史時，武懿宗討契丹，退保相州。

translations.literal: When serving as prefect, Wu Yizong campaigned against the Khitan and retreated to hold Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure as prefect, Wu Yizong fought the Khitan and fell back to defend Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後爭功殿中，懿宗陋短俯僂，頊嚴語侵之，無所容假。

translations.literal: Later they contended for merit in the hall. Yizong was short and stooped; Xu spoke harshly and insulted him, giving him no room.
translations.idiomatic: Later they contended for merit in the hall. Yizong was short and stooped; Xu spoke harshly and insulted him, giving him no quarter.

sentences.zh: 後怒曰：「我在，乃藉諸武，它日安可保？」

translations.literal: The empress angrily said, "While I live you rely on the Wu—on other days how can you be preserved?
translations.idiomatic: The empress angrily said, "While I live you rely on the Wu—on other days how can you be preserved?

sentences.zh: 銜之。

translations.literal: She harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she hated him.

sentences.zh: 張易之兄弟以寵盛，思自全，問頊計安出。

translations.literal: The Zhang Yizhi brothers, because favor was flourishing, thought to preserve themselves and asked Xu what plan to use.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang Yizhi brothers, at the height of favor, sought a way to survive and asked Xu what to do.

sentences.zh: 頊曰：「公家以幸進，非有大功於天下，勢必危。

translations.literal: Xu said, "Your house advanced through favor, not through great merit for the realm. Your position must be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Your house advanced through favor, not through great merit for the realm. Your position must be perilous.

sentences.zh: 吾有不朽策，願效之，非止保身，且世世不絕胙。」

translations.literal: Your subject has an immortal plan and wishes to offer it—not only to preserve the body, but to keep sacrificial meat for generation after generation."
translations.idiomatic: I have an immortal plan and wish to offer it—not only to preserve the body, but to keep sacrificial meat for generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 易之流涕請，頊曰：「天下思唐久矣！

translations.literal: Yizhi wept and begged. Xu said, "The realm has long yearned for Tang!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi wept and begged. Xu said, "The realm has long yearned for Tang!

sentences.zh: 廬陵斥外，相王幽閉。

translations.literal: Luling cast out abroad; the Prince of Xiang shut in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Luling was exiled abroad while the Prince of Xiang languished under guard.

sentences.zh: 上春秋高，武諸王，非海內屬意。

translations.literal: Sovereign's years are advanced; the Wu princes are not what the realm within favors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is advanced in years, and the Wu princes are not whom the empire would choose.

sentences.zh: 公盍從容請相王、廬陵，以副人望？

translations.literal: Why not at leisure ask for the Prince of Xiang and the Prince of Luling to meet the people's hope?
translations.idiomatic: Why not at leisure ask for the Prince of Xiang and the Prince of Luling to meet the people's hope?

sentences.zh: 易吊為賀之資也。」

translations.literal: That which turns condolence into congratulation is capital for it."
translations.idiomatic: That would give you the means to turn grief into celebration."

sentences.zh: 易之、昌宗乘間如頊教，後意乃定。

translations.literal: Yizhi and Changzong seized an opportunity as Xu taught and the empress's mind was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and Changzong seized an opportunity as Xu taught and the empress's mind was settled.

sentences.zh: 既而知頊與謀，召見問狀，頊對：「廬陵、相王皆陛下子，先帝顧托於陛下，當速有所付。」

translations.literal: When she learned Xu had joined the plot, she summoned him and asked the situation. Xu answered, "The Prince of Luling and the Prince of Xiang are both Your Majesty's sons. The late emperor entrusted them to Your Majesty—you should quickly decide whom to invest."
translations.idiomatic: When she learned Xu had joined the plot, she summoned him and asked the situation. Xu answered, "The Prince of Luling and the Prince of Xiang are both Your Majesty's sons. The late emperor entrusted them to Your Majesty—you should quickly decide whom to invest.

sentences.zh: 乃還中宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongzong was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhongzong was restored.

sentences.zh: 明年，頊坐弟冒偽官貶琰川尉，及辭，召見，泣曰：「臣去國，無復再謁，願有所言。

translations.literal: The next year Xu was demoted to magistrate of Yanchuan for his younger brother's false claim to office. When he took leave, he was summoned and wept, saying, "Your subject leaves the state and will never again attend audience. I wish to speak, yet my illness is urgent—I ask a moment's interval.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xu was demoted to magistrate of Yanchuan for his younger brother's false claim to office. When he took leave, he was summoned and wept, saying, "Your subject leaves the state and will never again attend audience. I wish to speak, yet my illness is urgent—I ask a moment's interval.

sentences.zh: 然疾棘，請須臾間。」

translations.literal: The empress ordered him seated. Xu said, "Are earth and water in one bowl in contention?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress ordered him seated. Xu said, "Are earth and water in one bowl in contention?"

sentences.zh: 後命坐，頊曰：「水土皆一盎，有爭乎？」

translations.literal: She said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "No."

translations.literal: He said, "If made into paste, is there contention?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If made into paste, is there contention?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「以為塗，有爭乎？」

translations.literal: She said, "No."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "No."

translations.literal: He said, "If the paste is made into Buddha and Dao, is there contention?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If the paste is made into Buddha and Dao, is there contention?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「以塗為佛與道，有爭乎？」

translations.literal: She said, "There is."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "There is."

sentences.zh: 曰：「有之。」

translations.literal: Xu bowed his head and said, "Even your subject thinks there is."
translations.idiomatic: Xu bowed his head and said, "Even your subject thinks there is."

sentences.zh: 頊頓首曰：「雖臣亦以為有。

translations.literal: Xu bowed his head and said, "Even your subject thinks there is.
translations.idiomatic: Xu bowed his head and said, "Even I think there is.

sentences.zh: 夫皇子、外戚，有分則兩安。

translations.literal: As for imperial sons and outer kin, if boundaries exist then both are secure.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the blood and maternal relatives can both live at ease only if their roles are clearly divided.

sentences.zh: 今太子再立，而外家諸王並封，陛下何以和之？

translations.literal: Now the crown prince has twice been established, and outer family princes are all enfeoffed—by what means will Your Majesty harmonize them?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has been restored twice, and every prince of the maternal line has been enfeoffed—how will you keep peace between them?

sentences.zh: 貴賤親疏之不明，是驅使必爭，臣知兩不安矣。」

translations.literal: If noble and base, close and distant are unclear, that drives them to contend. Your subject knows both will be insecure."
translations.idiomatic: If noble and base, close and distant are unclear, that drives them to contend. I know both will be insecure."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「朕知之，業已然，且奈何？」

translations.literal: The empress said, "I know it. The deed is already done—what then can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I know it. The deed is already done—what then can be done?"

sentences.zh: 頊尋徙始豐尉，客江都，卒。

translations.literal: Soon Xu was transferred to magistrate of Shifeng. As a guest in Jiangdu he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu was transferred to magistrate of Shifeng. As a guest in Jiangdu he died.

sentences.zh: 中宗之立，頊實倡之，會得罪，無知者。

translations.literal: Zhongzong's establishment—Xu in fact initiated it; happening to fall into guilt, none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had actually set Zhongzong on the throne, but after he fell from favor almost no one knew.

sentences.zh: 睿宗初，有發明其忠，乃下詔贈御史大夫。

translations.literal: Beginning of Ruizong, someone made manifest his loyalty; then issued edict posthumously granting censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ruizong's reign his loyalty came to light, and an edict posthumously made him censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：異乎，炎之暗於幾也！

translations.literal: Commentator says: Strange! Yan's darkness regarding the turning point!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: How strange—Pei Yan could not read the moment when fortune turned!

sentences.zh: 知中宗之不君，不知武後之盜朝，假虎翼而責其搏人，死固宜哉！

translations.literal: He knew Zhongzong was no fit ruler, yet did not know Empress Wu was usurping the court; he lent the tiger wings and then blamed it for mauling men—death was surely fitting!
translations.idiomatic: He knew Zhongzong was no fit ruler, yet did not see that Empress Wu was stealing the court; he lent the tiger its wings, then blamed it for mauling men—death was only fitting!

sentences.zh: 昭德、頊進不以道，君子恥之。

translations.literal: Zhaode and Xu advanced by improper means—the gentleman is ashamed of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode and Xu rose by unworthy means—a gentleman would be ashamed.

sentences.zh: 雖然，一情區區，抑武興唐，其助有端，則賢炎遠矣。

translations.literal: Even so, in their narrow private feelings they checked Wu and raised Tang; their help had its grounds—they were far worthier than Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, in their narrow private way they checked the Wu and raised the Tang; their help had its grounds—they were far worthier than Yan.

sentences.zh: 祎之、玄同漏言及誅，不失所以事君者雲。

translations.literal: Yizhi and Xuantong were executed for leaked words, yet did not lose what it means to serve a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and Xuantong were executed for words that leaked out, yet they never lost what it means to serve one's ruler.
